workstream: Wave 3C-2e — Private and public-access green-space reconciliation
scope: Research/classification only. No Civic Map assets are added or removed in this step.
purpose: Separate privately managed spaces that function as public-facing parks from gated/resident-oriented private community amenities, while preserving historical Makati inventory provenance.
classificationRules: The City Government of Makati 2020 private-park list is the historical named baseline.
Former Makati entries in the transferred Post Proper Northside geography remain historical records and are excluded from present-day Makati implementation.
Private ownership does not imply public access. Access class is determined separately from ownership/management.
Public-facing estate parks may enter the Civic Map private/public-access layer when current existence and management/access are sufficiently supported.
Residential-village parks remain in the audit even when current, but are not default Civic Map implementation candidates unless public access and civic usefulness are clearly established.
A current successor or rename is not asserted when the reviewed evidence only shows a nearby/redeveloped space.

baseline.source: Makati Facts and Figures 2020 — Private Parks

accessClasses.public-access-private-managed: Privately or estate managed but ordinarily intended for public visitors/users.
accessClasses.private-community-controlled: Village/community amenity with resident/guest or gate-controlled access; not treated as an ordinary public park.
accessClasses.access-or-current-identity-unresolved: Historical Makati private-park record whose present identity, access or successor cannot yet be frozen.
accessClasses.former-makati-now-taguig: Historical Makati inventory entry now outside present-day Makati.
